claims.statement: Choice blindness was named and demonstrated for switched face choices in 2005
claims.limit: laboratory face preferences only

claims.statement: Nobody notices when an outcome is swapped
claims.limit: detection occurs and rates depend on study conditions

claims.statement: In supermarket jam/tea study at most a third manipulated trials detected
claims.limit: Jam was tasted, tea smelled; detection included concurrent, retrospective and sensory-change reports; no universal consumer rate

claims.statement: 69 percent missed at least one of two moral-survey reversals
claims.limit: 69% missed at least one reversal; detection could mean correction of an apparently mistaken statement/rating relation, not identification of deception

claims.statement: 2013 paper reports Swedish 2010 election fieldwork with immediate stated voting intentions; does not establish durable election conversion
claims.decision: supported only for study date/context; reject election-effectiveness extrapolation
claims.limit: context-specific experimental responses not field effectiveness

claims.statement: 2013 pension choice study has 98 usable records
claims.limit: hypothetical portfolio not real pension transaction

claims.statement: Pension study proved actual portfolio money was moved
claims.limit: no real invested portfolio in experiment

claims.statement: Pension study aggregate detection bounds about 28.5–37.2% under assumptions, with dissimilar-condition upper bound 50%
claims.limit: 98 hypothetical portfolios; similar substitutions occurred first, dissimilar later, testing stopped after detection; upper estimates assumed early detectors would detect later unseen dissimilar swaps; not a clean similarity effect

claims.statement: Choice blindness is identical to change blindness
claims.limit: choice/action/feedback and visual scene change differ

claims.statement: Choice blindness validates clinical hypnosis
claims.limit: no therapy study

claims.statement: Paper purchase decision record is a proven debiasing treatment
claims.limit: proposed editorial aid, not experimentally validated

claims.statement: Puységur documents establish modern hypnotic audio efficacy
claims.limit: historical primary/secondary account, not audio trial

revision_note: R203 carries Praxxis reviewer corrections into R201 reader copy and R202 illusory truth wording/corrigendum. Applied corrections in isolated branch only. R204: incorporated Praxxis R203 full-text methods review: 2010 fieldwork versus 2013 election paper; jam taste versus tea smell and compound detection; moral survey rating/statement mismatch; pension order, stopping rule and assumption-dependent detection bounds. Source records are not independent study count.
